recentHooks.hook: You typed "AI Advantage Bootcamp Reddit" into the search bar because you wanted one thing the webinar would never give you: a stranger with nothing to sell.

Picture the two browser tabs open on your laptop right now.
Fifteen hours. That is the number the AI Advantage webinar dangles in front of you like a carrot on a stick. Fifteen hours a week, back in your pocket, for the low investment of $995.

You typed the program name into YouTube and got fourteen glowing reviews in a row, all wearing the same excited face, all using the same words, all linking to the same checkout page.
Remember when the answer to your money problems was supposed to be selling your own online course?
Dean Graziosi has sold something to almost everyone who has ever typed "how to make money online" into a search bar at 1am.
This is not the first time these two have stood on a stage together and pointed at a checkout button. Not even close.

Here is the question almost nobody asks out loud when a program gets a "2026 updated" label slapped on the sales page: did they rebuild the engine, or did they just repaint the car?
You sat through the webinar, the timer ticked toward zero, and somewhere around minute fifty a thought crossed your mind that you tried to push away: "I could probably just figure this out myself."
Can someone who still asks their kid to fix the TV remote actually learn AI in a six week program?
A guy worth tens of millions of dollars does not sit at his laptop typing prompts into ChatGPT at 11pm.
